title: The `until` Loop: Wait for Success 🚦
description: Loop until a condition becomes true. Learn when to flip the logic.

slides.title: `until` – The Opposite of `while` 🔄
slides.content:
## Loop Until True

`while` runs as long as the condition is **true**; `until` runs as long as the condition is **false**.

Syntax:
```bash
until [ condition ]; do
   commands
done
```
The loop stops when the condition becomes true.

slides.title: Count Up
slides.codeSnippet:
count=1
until [ $count -gt 5 ]; do
  echo "Count: $count"
  count=$((count + 1))
done

quizData.question: When does an `until` loop stop?

options.text: After a fixed number of iterations

quizData.explanation: `until` runs while the condition is false, so it stops when it finally becomes true.

slides.title: Practical `until` Examples 🔧
slides.content:
## Wait for Something

`until` is great for waiting:
- Wait for a file to appear: `until [ -f /tmp/ready ]; do sleep 1; done`
- Wait for network to come up: `until ping -c1 google.com; do sleep 5; done`

It clearly expresses the idea of "keep trying until successful".

slides.title: Wait for a File
slides.content: Pause script until a specific file exists:
slides.codeSnippet:
echo "Waiting for /tmp/go.txt..."
until [ -f /tmp/go.txt ]; do
  sleep 2
done
echo "File found, continuing."

quizData.question: An `until` loop will execute at least once even if the condition is initially true.
quizData.explanation: Like `while`, `until` checks the condition before the first iteration. If already true, the body is skipped entirely.

slides.title: Translating Between `while` and `until` 🔁
slides.content:
## Negate the Condition

```bash
# These two are equivalent:
while ! [ condition ]; do ... done
until [ condition ]; do ... done
```
Choose the one that reads more naturally for your scenario.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: If you find yourself writing `while ! ...`, consider `until` for readability.
